from output recovery, and claim C1 weakens.
Weekly research update · synthetic demo · version 0.1
cached features drift; correction moves them
Where we are, and what changed this week
Cached hidden features go stale over time, which means
that reusing them as a proxy for future features
drifts, and this is the core problem that motivates
Our method reuses a cached feature and then applies a
learned correction toward the future feature, and this
is what we have been building over the last few weeks.
The reuse-only baseline achieves a rollout cosine of
0.42, which is the number that we compare against in
Method v4 adds a correction objective and an
oracle diagnostic, and the question this week is
whether the correction actually moves toward the
future feature, or whether a different
downstream-valid direction is enough, and we
will look at both diagnostics today.
What changed in the method: v3 to v4
Version four adds a correction objective and an oracle diagnostic,
and it also scales down the correction magnitude, and these three
changes are what we will walk through on this slide.
We penalize deviation from the future feature so that the correction
is supervised directly, because otherwise the correction is only
indirectly supervised through the rollout metric.
We separate feature recovery from output recovery in order to test C1
and C2, because these two claims require different kinds of evidence
Reduce drift when the correction is applied over long rollouts.
Two stories for what the correction does
The first claim predicts that the correction vector aligns with the desired direction, so the residual between the corrected estimate and the desired
future feature would shrink over time.
Correction is nearly orthogonal to the desired direction
Same objects and positions as the previous slide; the measured dZ is ~90 degrees from desired.

from the cached feature to the future feature, and this is what we
measured with the cosine similarity above.
Output recovery may not require moving toward the exact future
hidden state, which suggests that an alternative representation

Comparison: competitor, last week, this week
Version four improves both downstream metrics over version three, and feature recovery stays low, and that is the
evidence behind the weakened C1 and the emerging C2, and it is not a hidden weakness that we are trying to conceal.
